Happy to fix it. I need a few specifics: which program are you using (Google Sheets, Excel), which columns are misaligned, and what the totals formula looks like now? If you paste the header row and one or two data rows, I can be exact.

google sheets. columns: school | category | tuition | aid | net price | score (1-4) | weight | weighted score

rows are 12 schools. 6 out of state, 4 UC, bayshore state, and one in-state polytechnic. the last two are the safeties

totals row says 0 for weighted score and net price is just showing text like 41200-18500

Two separate problems:

1. Net price showing as "41200-18500": that's text, not a formula. Retype it as =C2-D2 (starting with the equals sign), then drag down through row 13. Make sure tuition and aid are plain numbers, not text. Select C2:E13 and use Format > Number > Currency so they're consistent.

2. Weighted score total showing 0: the cells likely hold text, or your formula points at the wrong range. In H2 use =F2*G2 and fill down to H13. In the totals row (row 14), use =SUM(H2:H13). If the weights are percentages, check they add up to 100% with =SUM(G2:G13) in G14.

For alignment: select the whole table (A1:H14), then Format > Align > Horizontal. Left-align the text columns (A, B) and right-align the numeric ones (C through H). Center the score column (F) if you want it to look like a rubric. Header row: bold it, and use Format > Wrap text so long headers don't push columns wide. Then double-click the column border lines to auto-fit widths.

Since your rows are grouped by category, you could also add a thin border between groups: out-of-state (rows 2-7), UC (8-11), then the two safeties (12-13).

ok net price works now. but it has to look like a rubric, grace will nitpick every single cell. her rubrics have a shaded header, thin gridlines, and the score column centered with the points possible in a row at the bottom. if one thing is off she will find it

Here's a rubric-style setup:

- Header row: select A1:H1, fill with a mid-gray (or dark blue with white text), bold, centered vertically and horizontally.
- Gridlines: select A1:H14, then the borders button > All borders, thin, light gray or black.
- Score column (F): center-aligned, and format as plain number (Format > Number > Number, 0 decimals).
- Points possible row: add it in row 15. Put "Points possible" in A15, then 4 in F15 and the maximum weighted score in H15 using =F15*SUM(G2:G13) if your weights sum to 1, or adjust to match your scale. Make this row italic so it reads as a footer.
- Totals row (14): bold, with a thicker top border so it separates from the data.
- Consistency: make sure the font and size are the same throughout (Select all, then set one font). Nitpickers notice mixed fonts and decimal places fast, so set all currency columns to 0 decimals.
- Freeze the header: View > Freeze > 1 row.

If you want to check for stray errors before printing, use Edit > Find and replace and search for "#" to catch any error cells.
